title: Summit Loan Terms Fixed at Closing
content:
A Cedarline Summit Proprietary Reverse Mortgage loan is boarded with the terms fixed at closing. Each term below is read against the plan of the loan.

## Article 1 — Borrower, home and amount

1.1 The youngest borrower was at least the plan's minimum age, or the lower age the plan's state schedule gives for the property state.

1.2 The home was appraised at least at the plan's minimum home value, using the plan's number of appraisals at closing.

1.3 The initial principal limit is at most the plan's maximum percentage of the appraised value, and at most the plan's maximum loan amount.

1.4 At least the plan's minimum initial draw percentage of the principal limit was drawn at closing.

1.5 The origination fee was the plan's origination fee percentage of the principal limit, capped at the plan's origination fee cap, financed from proceeds where the plan allows closing costs to be paid from loan proceeds.

## Article 2 — Lien, property and title

2.1 The loan holds the lien position of its plan.

2.2 Only the Summit Second Lien may sit behind an existing forward first mortgage.

2.3 A condominium without FHA approval is eligible only under a plan that accepts it.

2.4 Title may be held in a revocable living trust, as the plan provides.

## Article 3 — Servicing features

3.1 Every Summit loan is enrolled in annual occupancy certification.

3.2 A Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve may be set up at closing where the plan provides that option.

3.3 Cedarline may advance unpaid property charges, as the plan provides.

3.4 A surviving non-borrowing spouse may remain where the plan carries the spouse protection rider.

3.5 Payoffs are available under the payoff plans the plan lists, a retaining heir paying on the plan's heir payoff basis.

3.6 Interest follows the plan's interest accrual method and accrual rounding.

3.7 A draw returned by the receiving bank is handled as the plan's returned-draw terms provide, with no ledger entry until it is reissued.

## Reading Article 1 against a hypothetical file

For illustration only: a home appraised at USD 1215000.00 under a plan whose maximum percentage were 50% supports a principal limit of at most USD 607500.00, unless the plan's maximum loan amount is lower, in which case that amount is the limit; both ceilings hold at once. A principal limit of USD 600000.00 under a plan with a 1.5% origination fee and a USD 20000.00 cap carries a fee of USD 9000.00, below the cap.

## Reading Article 3.7

A draw returned by the receiving bank leaves no entry on the loan ledger while it is outstanding; the entry appears only when the draw is reissued.
